I will stay with the wheat-maize rotation on the full 12.0 mu. On land like mine in Quzhou, with well irrigation, I do not like to gamble on a weak fertilizer plan. I start from what has held yield before, then I adjust by target yield and soil pull. For winter wheat, I will push nitrogen a bit harder because tillering and grain filling decide whether I make money or just cover costs. I will keep phosphorus steady for rooting, and I will not skip potassium because lodging and grain fill suffer when I do. I will irrigate three times if water timing is normal: once after sowing or at establishment if moisture is short, once at jointing, and once around heading to grain filling. For summer maize, I will use less total nitrogen than wheat but still enough to hold ear size, and I will keep phosphorus and potassium in because straw removal and repeated cropping pull nutrients every year. I will do maize with no-tillage after wheat harvest to save time and keep moisture, because with only two people in the household, labor efficiency matters. I would rather spend a little more on fertilizer than lose yield across 12 mu; that is the bigger risk for me.
